Image sets, local folders & reconstruction error

SetFolderDimensionsPixels / imageStorageMean reprojection error
(input-image px)		Full-resolution equivalent
(px)

Every folder contains frame_0001.png through frame_0500.png. Reductions use Lanczos directly from the full-resolution masters. A 2× reduction halves both dimensions.

Final error after refinement. Both error columns use the largest registered component after bundle adjustment and observation filtering. Reprojection error measures how far reconstructed points project from observed image features; lower values mean tighter image fit. The full-resolution equivalent multiplies the input-image error by the downsample factor (1, 2, 4 or 8), so every residual uses the same pixel scale. One 8× image pixel corresponds to eight full-resolution pixels.

These models do not share identical features or observations: the 8× main component registers 343/500 frames, while the others register 492–493/500. This is a comparison of image fit, not a measurement of dense-cloud, mesh or real-world room accuracy; those require reference geometry. Values display six decimal places; the measured-results JSON retains full precision.

Image resolution and reconstruction counts

500 INPUT FRAMES AT EACH SCALE

These are measured totals from the saved COLMAP databases and point clouds. The sparse count is for the main component; the dense count is the complete fused cloud. Each panel has its own vertical scale. X positions follow the numeric downsample factors (1, 2, 4, 8); each chart reports Pearson r against that factor (n = 4).

Loading measured chart data…

Fewer input pixels produce fewer detected features and reconstructed points in this run, but counts alone do not measure geometric accuracy. In the labels, 8× means each image dimension is reduced to one-eighth: 270 × 480 pixels, or 1/64 as many pixels per frame as full resolution. The correlation is descriptive for these four reconstructions, not a general accuracy score.

HOW TO READ THESE RESULTS

Coverage matters as much as detail.

Each resolution is reconstructed independently. Models have arbitrary scale and coordinate systems; they are not aligned. Dense processing uses the largest registered component. Other non-empty sparse components can be inspected in the viewer above.

A plain-wall transition around 32 seconds has weak feature overlap. Windows, mirrors, clear chairs, and occluded surfaces remain difficult. A completed pipeline is not proof of a complete or metrically accurate room.
